item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 9, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Audacy has a new morning team at New York's legendary WCBS-FM. Veteran broadcasters Trey Morgan and Loren Raye will host weekdays from six to ten. Morgan brings experience from major markets nationwide, while Raye is a two-time Gracie Award winner. The pair will lead mornings on one of America's top Classic Hits stations.
From the radio side of the industry, The Alliance for Women in Media Foundation has opened entries for the 52nd Annual Gracie Awards. Eligible television, radio, streaming, podcast and digital work from 2026 can compete, with an early-bird deadline of December 10. National winners will be honored next May in Beverly Hills.
Turning to radio, NBCUniversal is accepting applications for its Spring 2027 Page Program through October 19. The paid program gives early-career professionals three rotational assignments across NBCUniversal businesses in New York or Universal City, California. The new class begins January 25. Candidates can submit an application through the NBCUniversal Careers Page Program site.
On the TV side, Gray Media is expanding free local access to Minnesota Timberwolves basketball. Stations in four Minnesota and Wisconsin markets will simulcast 15 games this season under a new agreement with TEGNA and DAZN, with select games also airing on Gray’s major network affiliates.
Turning to television, Two stars of A Different World are getting back together! Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell are launching A Different World View, a new weekly podcast from iHeartMedia's Black Effect Podcast Network. The show premieres October 15, with Debbie Allen as the first guest. Expect behind-the-scenes stories, laughs and plenty of nostalgia.
In radio news, Zixi has named John Towers its new Chief Financial Officer. Towers brings more than 20 years of experience, including leadership positions at Sony, Deluxe and Fabric Data. He'll oversee financial operations as Zixi expands its technology for broadcasters and streaming companies moving from traditional satellite distribution to IP-based video delivery.
Next, Boston-based GBH is welcoming three new trustees as it celebrates its 75th anniversary. Ingrid Chung of Fidelity Investments, Jonathan Goldstein of TA Associates, and John Kennedy of UMass Amherst join the board, bringing experience in finance, education and journalism. The appointments come as GBH continues expanding its public media services.
And finally, The Academy is now accepting media credential applications for the 99th Oscars, happening March 14, 2027. News organizations can apply for in-person or virtual backstage Interview Room access. Applications must be submitted by November 23 at 5 p.m. Pacific. Visit press dot oscars dot org for details.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
